optionReasons.saa-ini-131:option:0: The highest instance connected 24/7 is the opposite of automatic adjustment — maximum waste in idle hours.
optionReasons.saa-ini-131:option:1: Pre-peak manual replicas require manual forecasting and work — and scale LEITURA, not the overall computing capacity.
optionReasons.saa-ini-131:option:3: The DynamoDB is not relational — the requirement requires compatibility MySQL/PostgreSQL.

finalJustifications: Because Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts the capacity in ACUs up and down in seconds, following demand, without manual provisioning.
Because Serverless v2 turns off the bank at night and reconnects in the morning in scheduled windows, charging only commercial hours.
Because Serverless v2 converts the bank to a model NoSQL during peaks, absorbing the load without changing the application.
Because Serverless v2 charges a monthly fixed value calibrated by the average use, protecting the budget from daily variations.

optionReasons.saa-ini-132:option:0: GSIs create alternate query paths — do not fix the bad partition key distribution of the table.
optionReasons.saa-ini-132:option:1: Sort key organizes items DENTRO of a partition — does not resolve the concentration in few partitions.
optionReasons.saa-ini-132:option:3: Streams captures changes for consumers — does not cause throttling of writing.

finalJustifications: ♪ 'Cause I'm alone ♪ 3 key values focus everything on few physical partitions ('hot partitions') — the partition key needs to ALTA cardinality to spread items.
Because DynamoDB limits each table to three physical partitions by default, and the increase requires opening a support ticket.
Because the provided capacity is only valid for the first partition created — the others inherit only the remaining stock capacity.
Because text partition keys are slower than numeric keys: string hash costs more and delays recordings.

optionReasons.saa-ini-134:option:0: No write-behind ESCRITA is born in the cache and then goes to the bank — the scenario describes reading with cache miss.
optionReasons.saa-ini-134:option:2: TTL infinite is expiration policy, not a loading strategy.
optionReasons.saa-ini-134:option:3: In write-through the cache is updated NA ESCRITA — the scenario carries the data in the LEITURA after the miss.

finalJustifications: Because in lazy loading (cache-aside) the data only enters the cache when requested and not found: miss → search the bank → saves to the cache for the next ones.
Because in lazy loading the bank only replicates the data to the background cache, keeping the hot items preloaded.
Because lazy loading ensures that the cache never gets outdated: each miss revalidates the data against the origin before serving.
Because lazy loading writes in the cache and the bank at the same time, ensuring immediate consistency between the two layers.

optionReasons.saa-ini-147:option:1: The DAX speed up readings in UMA region — players from other continents would continue to cross the ocean.
optionReasons.saa-ini-147:option:2: More capacity does not change the PHYSICAL: the intercontinental latency remains.
optionReasons.saa-ini-147:option:3: There is no 'Read Replica' in DynamoDB — multi-region replication is the role of Global Tables.

finalJustifications: Because Global Tables replicate the table in active-active mode between the Regions: each accepts readings and local writings, spread to the others in seconds.
Because the Global Tables route all the writings to a single master region, which spreads them to local reading replicas.
Because the Global Tables use the CloudFront to serve the items on the edge, approaching the score of players from each continent.
Because the Global Tables keep copies read only in the secondary regions, promoted to main during peaks.

optionReasons.saa-ini-150:option:2: Daily manual adjustment is just what you want to eliminate — and fail at peaks out of time.

finalJustifications: Because Aurora Auto Scaling add/remove Aurora Replicas automatically based on metrics policy as CPU or connections — number follows demand.
Because Aurora Auto Scaling resizes the type of the writer instance in peaks, raising the cluster reading capacity.
Because Aurora Auto Scaling migrate replicas to cheaper regions outside business hours, cutting the cost of the morning.
Because Aurora Auto Scaling is the commercial name of the serverless mode, which dimension the ACUs of the writer according to the demand for reading.

optionReasons.saa-ini-152:option:0: Replicas without cluster scale mode LEITURA — all writings remain in a single primary and memory is not partitioned.
optionReasons.saa-ini-152:option:1: The DAX is cached from DynamoDB — does not replace a Redis cluster.
optionReasons.saa-ini-152:option:2: A larger node is scale VERTICAL ceiling — does not partition data or distribute writings.

finalJustifications: Because Cluster Mode partitions data into multiple shards, each with its primary — climbing storage and writing horizontally.
Because Cluster Mode duplicates the entire dataset in each shard, ensuring total cache redundancy between the groups of us.
Because Cluster Mode switches the engine to Memcached internally, the only one capable of partitioning data between multiple nodes.
Because Cluster Mode extends memory to volumes EBS attached, exceeding the physical limit of a node without partitioning.

optionReasons.saa-ini-155:option:2: The Trusted Advisor checks good accounting practices — does not analyse SQL individual.
optionReasons.saa-ini-155:option:3: CPUtilization alarm warns QUE the bank is overloaded — does not identify QUAIS SQLs cause load.

finalJustifications: Because Performance Insights shows DB Load on a visual panel and ranks the wants SQL, hosts and users who contribute most to the load in the period.
Because Performance Insights automatically rewrites the identified slow queries, applying the optimization hints.
Because Performance Insights automatically creates indexes by detecting full table scans at bench slow times.
Because Performance Insights is exclusive to Aurora, whose distributed storage provides the loading metrics per query.

optionReasons.saa-ini-187:option:2: Auto Scaling reacting after 1 HORA would let the throttling happen all along the sudden peak.

finalJustifications: Because On-Demand charges for request made and instantly scales for unpredictable peaks — no risk of throttling by sub-supply or idle fixed cost.
Because On-Demand guarantees unlimited capacity free of charge in the former 3 months, the calibration period for new tables in production.
Because On-Demand automatically supplies twice the highest historical peak, keeping the rest that avoids any throttling.
Because On-Demand exchanges the minimum one-year commitment for lower fees per request — the reserve model of the DynamoDB.
